result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B puts lending and returning side by side with one-click Take back, and its due-back date is a normal date field labeled as a one-week default you can change, which fits item 4 well. A has a stronger member-lookup flow with tabs, but it offers 3/7/14-day loan lengths without saying they are defaults. That reads as an invented policy, and A also mixes 'borrower' and 'member'. Neither screenshot shows the edge-case messages, and B's free-text borrower field gives no clear member-not-found path. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B has a real member lookup (name or phone, showing what each member has out and any overdue tools), a numbered lend flow and a separate take-back tab, so it covers the whole 'find a member, then finish a lend or return' flow better. A's member field is plain text with no lookup, so there is no 'member not found' case, and it mixes 'Borrower' with 'member'. A handles policy better, though: its due-back date is clearly labeled as a default and can be changed, while B's 3/7/14-day loan options look like made-up loan lengths, and B also mixes terms (borrowing, free, late).
